key_insight: An adsorbate-free graph neural network screens dissociative water adsorption on nickel using only bare-metal geometries and candidate binding-site anchors.
engineering_relevance: The framework enables efficient screening of OH*+H* adsorption configurations on nickel nanoparticles up to approximately 3,000 atoms without constructing or relaxing adsorbates during screening.
method: Define candidate O- and H-binding sites as sets of nickel anchor atoms.
Build graphs from anchors and their local nickel environments in MACE-relaxed bare structures.
Use separate GNNs to predict DFT-reference adsorption energies and binding-site retention after relaxation.
evidence_signal: The energy model achieves 0.031 eV internal-validation MAE, with independent tests on unseen Ni55, Ni91, Ni130 clusters and larger surface cells supporting transferability, especially for relative-energy ranking.
watch_item: Quantitative accuracy varies across systems; treat the retention classifier as a conservative filter rather than a guarantee of site stability.
paper_title: Adsorbate-Free Screening of Dissociative Water Adsorption on Nickel Nanoparticles via Graph Neural Networks
